entries.summary: Bearish elevated-downside-risk outlook remains unchanged from 05:51 EST. Fresh Friday pre-PPI reporting places the 10Y Treasury near 5.130% and 2Y near 4.861%, an approximately +26.9bp spread, confirming continued elevated duration pressure without synchronized QQQ/SOX evidence. Reuters reports Nasdaq-100 futures -0.11%, NVDA +1.8% premarket and MSFT -2.6% premarket; underlying quote timestamps are not matched. October PPI remains scheduled for 08:30 EST, with no actual release yet. Open Watch remains at 162 events as of repository 08:28 UTC update. Friday cash SOX, breadth, VXN/VIX and live CME FedWatch remain unverified.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
Friday Reuters oil report indicates Brent and WTI declined versus the previous reported session; if sustained, this could relieve inflation pressure, but this is not an observed US equity response.
New SMIC foundry commentary indicates persistent AI demand and supply tightness through 2027, a long-horizon demand/pricing signal rather than a confirmed immediate SOX catalyst.
Cerebras raised 2026 revenue guidance and announced Microsoft cloud deal, supporting AI-compute demand, without verified immediate QQQ/SOX impact.
A contemporaneous WSJ Asian-session report describes a tentative Asian chip-stock rebound; not confirmation of US semiconductor recovery.
Reuters Friday report indicates NVDA +1.8% premarket; no cash-session confirmation.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

Reuters November 13 Asian-session coverage describes higher US yields and Nvidia-linked weakness across Asia, consistent with persistent duration and leadership risk; no matched Friday US QQQ/SOX confirmation.
SMIC says AI chip capacity may stay constrained through 2027, which may increase costs and delivery delays even as demand remains robust.
November 13 01:14 ET Investing.com report describes US equity futures turning lower, without verified matched index/semiconductor prices.
WSJ Friday Asian-session 10Y yield of 5.128% and 2Y 4.861% reinforce elevated discount-rate risk; data are not synchronized with US stock trading.
Reuters Friday report indicates MSFT -2.6% premarket amid prolonged service outages; sustained index impact not verified.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq/QQQ enters Friday under elevated downside risk following Thursday's -0.39% Nasdaq and -0.54% SOX closes, with Nvidia -4.34% despite selective AMD and Broadcom strength. Reuters Friday premarket Nasdaq-100 futures -0.11%, NVDA +1.8% and MSFT -2.6% are indicative and asynchronous. October PPI has not been released at this checkpoint. Friday Treasury commentary indicates 10Y 5.130% and 2Y 4.861%, a correctly computed 26.9bp curve spread. Elevated discount rates and uncertain AI leadership remain the principal risks.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the 05:51 EST assessment, a newer published Treasury pair (10Y 5.130%, 2Y 4.861%) supports the same high-rate backdrop and implies +26.9bp versus the earlier rounded +27bp. This is not a meaningful directional shift. Open Watch's last verified repository update remains 162 events at 08:28 UTC. No verified new event or synchronized equity/volatility reading changes the outlook.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The negative Nasdaq/SOX cash closes and Nvidia weakness signal fragile leadership, although AMD and Broadcom's Thursday gains argue against indiscriminate semiconductor selling. Higher Treasury yields weigh on long-duration growth multiples. The premarket Nvidia rebound and Microsoft decline are not confirmed regular-session market responses. Expected PPI impact must remain conditional until actual data and ensuing cross-asset price reaction are observed.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13 is dominated by the 08:30 EST October PPI release and the first synchronized rates/QQQ/SOX/breadth response after 09:30. Monday November 16 should reveal whether Friday's response persists or reverses. Tuesday November 17 adds earnings and event risk, including Nvidia earnings timing that requires independent confirmation. Base case remains volatile, downside-skewed consolidation rather than a confirmed directional breakdown.
editorial.bullCase: Benign PPI, falling matched Treasury yields, sustained Nvidia stabilization, semiconductor outperformance and expanding Nasdaq breadth could turn Thursday's partial recovery into a durable rebound. Positive AMAT and Cisco earnings support the underlying AI-infrastructure demand thesis but have not yet demonstrated index-wide follow-through.
editorial.bearCase: Hotter PPI or hawkish repricing could push 2Y/10Y yields higher and pressure expensive growth equities. Renewed Nvidia-led SOX weakness, weak breadth, rising VXN/VIX and persistent oil inflation pressure would reinforce the downside path. The Microsoft outage-related premarket drop is a potential additional drag, not yet confirmed in cash trading.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the actual October PPI at BLS 08:30 EST; compare headline/core details with consensus and observe the synchronized 2Y/10Y, QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, Nvidia, breadth and VXN/VIX response after cash open. Recheck Brent/WTI with source timestamps, CME FedWatch and the curated Open Watch feed. Avoid treating asynchronous published indications as simultaneous signals.
